stem: Let $X$ be the set of the integers from {=p} to {=last}, that is, $X$ has {=n} elements. The product $X\times X$ is represented by an arrow diagram, where each ordered pair is an arrow and a pair whose first projection equals its second projection is drawn as a buttonhole (an arrow that starts and ends at the same point). How many of the arrows are NOT buttonholes?
solution: $X\times X$ has {=n}$\times${=n}$={=n*n}$ ordered pairs, so the diagram has {=n*n} arrows.
The pairs with equal projections are $(x, x)$, one for each element of $X$, so there are {=n} buttonholes.
notes: Advanced: counting with the buttonhole idea from book example 5.
